title: ECTODERMAL DYSPLASIA 17 WITH OR WITHOUT LIMB MALFORMATIONS

relationships.phenotype: ECTODERMAL DYSPLASIA 17 WITH OR WITHOUT LIMB MALFORMATIONS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the LEF1 gene. Heterozygous deletions encompassing LEF1 have also been reported in patients with ectodermal dysplasia.

checks.claim: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the LEF1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Our findings establish mono- and biallelic variants in LEF1 as a cause for a novel syndrome comprising limb malformations and ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract says mono- and biallelic variants, not heterozygous or homozygous. The biallelic variant was found in a consanguineous family, but the abstract does not say it was homozygous.

checks.claim: Heterozygous deletions encompassing LEF1 have been reported in patients with ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: We report two unrelated patients with 4q25 de novo deletion encompassing LEF1, associated with severe oligodontia of primary and permanent dentition, hypotrichosis and hypohidrosis compatible with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The deletions are framed as LEF1 haploinsufficiency, which means they are heterozygous.

paragraphs.text: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is a disorder caused by variants in LEF1, which encodes a transcription factor acting downstream of the WNT-beta-catenin signaling pathway. Its phenotypic spectrum includes ectodermal dysplasia and various limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly, or split hand/foot (Dufour et al., 2022). Ectodermal features reported include severe oligodontia of primary and permanent dentition, hypotrichosis, and hypohidrosis (Levy et al., 2020).

checks.explanation: The paper establishes LEF1 variants as the cause. The name ECTD17 does not appear in the abstract, which calls it 'a new syndrome' (title) and 'a novel syndrome' (conclusion).

paragraphs.text: In 2 unrelated patients with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, Levy et al. (2020) identified de novo deletions of chromosome 4q25 encompassing the LEF1 gene. The authors noted that no pathogenic variants involving LEF1 had previously been reported in humans and concluded that LEF1 haploinsufficiency plays a role in ectodermal dysplasia.

paragraphs.text: Using high-throughput sequencing, Dufour et al. (2022) detected monoallelic variants in LEF1 in 11 affected individuals from 4 unrelated families, and a biallelic variant in an affected individual from a consanguineous family. Cellular consequences were characterized by immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, pulldown assays, and/or RNA sequencing. Functional data indicated 2 molecular mechanisms: haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding, and loss of beta-catenin binding caused by biallelic variants. Transcriptomic studies revealed an alteration of WNT signaling.

agent.process_note: All four files were read in full. Three are abstracts only and Hassan et al. (2024) is a title only. None of them gives specific nucleotide or protein changes, so no allelic variants could be curated. No gene MIM number or chromosomal location was supplied, so the intro leaves them out. The papers disagree on the deletion locus: Levy et al. give 4q25, while the Dufour et al. abstract refers to '4q35 microdeletions'. Galceran et al. (2004) covers Lef1 and Dll1 in mouse somitogenesis, not ectodermal dysplasia, so it was left uncited.
